tasks.title: Add read-only squash mergeability preflight
tasks.description: Implement a shared WorktreeManager mergeability preflight that checks whether the current issue branch can be squash-merged into the current base branch without mutating either branch. The result must include the merge identity and conflict evidence needed by Check, approval validation, and Integrate.
acceptanceCriteria: Preflight runs an equivalent `git merge --squash <candidate>` attempt in disposable state and does not advance or dirty the base branch or issue branch
A clean candidate returns `canMerge: true` with `strategy`, `targetBranch`, `baseSha`, `candidateHeadSha`, `mergeBaseSha`, `conflictFiles`, and `checkedAt` populated
A conflicting candidate returns `canMerge: false` with structured conflict files captured before cleanup
Temporary worktree or merge state cleanup is best-effort and cleanup failure does not convert a detected conflict into a pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Produces the shared MergeabilitySnapshot contract and checkSquashMergeability API consumed by all later tasks.

tasks.title: Make merge-ready use squash preflight
tasks.description: Update the Check-stage merge-ready behavior to project the shared squash preflight result instead of inferring readiness from fast-forward or current rebase conflict state. Ensure any active legacy merge-readiness path delegates to the same preflight or no longer makes independent pass decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: `merge-ready` passes only when the preflight snapshot has `canMerge: true`
`merge-ready` fails for a branch whose final squash merge would conflict even when ordinary worktree `conflictingFiles` is empty
Check output includes structured mergeability facts including base/head/merge-base SHAs, target branch, strategy, canMerge, and conflict files
No active merge-readiness path keeps the old `conflictingFiles.length === 0` inference as a proof of mergeability
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes the preflight API and produces the user-visible Check gate evidence.

tasks.title: Bind Check approval to mergeability snapshot
tasks.description: Persist the latest passing merge-ready snapshot in Check approval output and validate that snapshot before approval can enqueue Integrate. Approval must fail closed when the snapshot is missing, failing, or no longer matches the current base, candidate head, merge base, or target branch.
acceptanceCriteria: Check approval output includes the latest passing `mergeReadySnapshot` alongside existing review approval evidence
Approval rejects missing, malformed, or `canMerge: false` merge-ready snapshots
Approval returns a stale-state failure when current base SHA, candidate head SHA, merge-base SHA, or target branch differs from the approved snapshot
Approval does not rerun preflight and silently approve a different candidate than the one presented to the user
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes the merge-ready check output from T-002 and produces approval-time staleness validation.

tasks.title: Preflight Integrate before delivery side effects
tasks.description: Add an Integrate-stage guard that validates approved mergeability evidence before spec sync, archive, or merge tasks mutate project state. If evidence is absent or stale, Integrate must run one fresh squash preflight and stop with clear diagnostics when the candidate cannot merge or must be rechecked.
acceptanceCriteria: Integrate validates mergeability before `integrate:spec-sync`, `integrate:archive-change`, and `integrate:merge` side effects
Missing or stale approved mergeability evidence prevents side-effectful delivery and reports that Check must be rerun when the approved candidate changed
A fresh Integrate preflight failure stops Integrate with structured base/head/merge-base, strategy, target branch, canMerge, and conflict file evidence
A valid current snapshot allows Integrate to continue to existing delivery steps without changing workflow status semantics
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes approval snapshot validation from T-003 and protects Integrate side effects.

tasks.title: Report structured final merge conflicts
tasks.description: Keep the actual Integrate squash merge as the final authority while improving its failure evidence for post-preflight races. When the real merge fails, capture conflict files and merge identity details before cleanup so users can diagnose conflicts that appear after preflight.
acceptanceCriteria: `mergeApprovedCandidate()` still runs the real `git merge --squash <candidate>` as the authoritative delivery merge
Final merge failure output includes target branch, strategy, conflict files, and available base/head/merge-base SHAs
Conflict files are collected before cleanup or abort removes the evidence
A race after preflight is reported as a failed `integrate:merge` task with structured conflict diagnostics
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes the Integrate preflight path from T-004 but preserves the real merge as final authority.

tasks.title: Expose persisted mergeability evidence
tasks.description: Ensure structured merge-ready and Integrate preflight evidence is preserved in workflow run records and remains visible through existing diagnostics surfaces. The stored Check approval evidence must remain distinct from any refreshed Integrate preflight diagnostics so stale approval cannot be silently replaced.
acceptanceCriteria: Check-stage records preserve the merge-ready snapshot fields needed for approval validation and user diagnostics
Integrate preflight diagnostics are recorded when Integrate refreshes missing or stale evidence
API, CLI, logs, and UI consumers can read the persisted mergeability facts through existing workflow evidence surfaces without recomputing mergeability
Refreshed Integrate diagnostics do not overwrite the user-approved Check mergeReadySnapshot
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes Check, approval, and Integrate mergeability outputs and makes the persisted evidence consistently available.

tasks.title: Cover mergeability and staleness regressions
tasks.description: Add regression coverage for the #207 failure class and stale mergeability evidence. Tests should include real Git fixtures for squash-merge conflicts plus workflow/API coverage for approval and Integrate stale-snapshot handling.
acceptanceCriteria: A real Git regression test proves `merge-ready` fails when final squash merge conflicts while ordinary worktree conflict files are empty
A clean squash-mergeable candidate test proves the snapshot includes required mergeability facts
Approval staleness tests prove base, candidate head, merge-base, and target-branch changes reject old merge-ready evidence
Integrate tests prove missing or stale mergeability evidence stops before side-effectful spec sync/archive work
Final merge race coverage proves structured conflict files are reported when the authoritative merge fails after preflight
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Consumes all implemented behavior and verifies the end-to-end regression class.
